items.question: Under what conditions must a certain teaching remain concealed rather than openly disclosed in the mortal world?
premises: A teaching is marked as something to be concealed.
Concealment is to be carried out with effort.
Such concealment is prescribed specifically among the lowest of men in the mortal world.
items.inference: The teaching is to be guarded with effort and restricted to context among the lowest of men.
uncertainties: Extent of restriction not specified
items.plain_english: This teaching is to be concealed with effort in the mortal world, especially among the lowest of men.

items.question: To whom and under what test condition must a particular gift be offered rather than given indiscriminately?
premises: A particular item is marked as something to be given.
It is to be given only to one who has been previously accomplished.
That recipient or item is to be tested for the span of one year.
items.inference: The gift is reserved for a previously accomplished person who has been tested for one year.
uncertainties: Direction of testing remains unspecified
items.plain_english: What is to be given should go to one previously accomplished and tested for one year.

items.question: By what origin is a particular chapter identified as holding its place in a sequence of instruction?

items.inference: The fifth chapter is identified as one that emerged from Candradvīpa.
uncertainties: Content relation to Candradvīpa not specified
items.plain_english: The fifth chapter emerged from Candradvīpa.

items.question: By what means does a speaker claim to have come to know the determination of Kaula?
premises: The speaker addresses the lord of Kaulas.
The speaker claims to have become known or to know through another's grace.
That knowledge is specified as the determination of Kaula.
The agent of that knowledge is the speaker.
items.inference: By the grace of the lord of Kaulas, the speaker has come to know the determination of Kaula.
uncertainties: Ambiguity between jñāta as known and as knower remains
items.plain_english: By your grace, O lord of Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of Kaula.

items.question: What two points of inquiry must be settled to determine both which entity is called the soul and what its nature is?
premises: An inquiry is made as to which soul is declared.
A disjunctive inquiry is made as to what the nature of the soul is.
Both inquiries concern the same entity designated as the soul.
items.inference: The question requires identifying the declared soul and specifying its nature.
uncertainties: No answer is given in this verse
items.plain_english: Which soul is declared? Or what is the nature of the soul?

rows.grounds: interrogative pronoun with sandhi fusion as given

items.question: What must be specified to answer where all things go to dissolution and to have that full account disclosed?
premises: An inquiry is made as to in what all things go to dissolution.
The particle ca-eva marks that inquiry as emphatic.
A request is made to tell all of that to the speaker.
items.inference: A full account is requested of the locus in which all things undergo dissolution.
uncertainties: Locus of dissolution not specified in this verse
items.plain_english: And indeed, in what does all this go to dissolution? Tell me all of that.

items.question: What set of attributes must belong to the entity designated as that supreme one to distinguish it as partless and unconditioned?
premises: A single entity is designated by saḥ.
That entity is supreme, partless, and eternal.
That entity is further free from disease and stainless.
items.inference: The designated entity is characterized by a cluster of negating and positive attributes as supreme, partless, eternal, free from disease, and stainless.
uncertainties: Syntactic role of paraṃ remains ambiguous between adjective and adverb
items.plain_english: He is the supreme, partless, eternal one, free from disease and stainless.

items.question: What identity relation must hold between the soul, the haṃsa, and power as an individual to mark one as supreme over the other?
premises: He is the soul and is supreme.
A relative clause identifies who is meant by that supremacy.
That same entity is he, the haṃsa, and is designated as power as an individual.
items.inference: The supreme soul is identified with the haṃsa and with power as an individual.
uncertainties: Exact force of parataro relative to jīva remains open
items.plain_english: He is the soul, the supreme one. Indeed, he who is that is the haṃsa, power as an individual.

items.question: In what locus must a wind-filled air be situated to account for its presence in relation to all beings?
premises: There is an air that is wind-filled.

items.inference: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.
uncertainties: Grammatical agreement between vāyuḥ and saṃsthitam remains open
items.plain_english: The wind-filled air is situated in all beings.

items.question: Under what minimal condition is a particular entity called supreme Śiva rather than under a condition of continued embodiment?

items.inference: Upon merely leaving the body, that entity is called supreme Śiva.
uncertainties: Force of mātra as mere or sufficient remains open
items.plain_english: Upon merely leaving the body, he is called supreme Śiva.

items.question: What kind of object is said to be heard abiding in the ear when it is transmitted through a continuous tradition?

items.inference: What abides in the ear and comes down through tradition is heard, as addressed to the goddess.
uncertainties: Whether the object is sound or teaching remains open
items.plain_english: O goddess, what abides in the ear and has come down through tradition is heard.

items.question: By what means alone is a result said to be attained when addressed to one of fair face?

uncertainties: The specific result attained is not stated in this verse
items.plain_english: By this mere knowledge, and by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.

items.question: What practice over what time is enjoined for one who takes up an ochre robe free from bondage?

items.inference: One who takes up the ochre robe free from bondage should practice for six months.
uncertainties: Object of abhyas remains syntactically open
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who takes up the ochre robe free from bondage should practice from six months onward.

items.question: What state follows for one freed from all diseases in relation to yogis and union with them?

items.inference: One freed from all diseases attains union together with yogis.
uncertainties: Syntactic link between all three elements remains open
items.plain_english: Freed from all diseases, one attains union together with yogis.

items.question: What claim is made about a particular practice of the soul when addressed to Bhairavī?

items.plain_english: This practice of the soul has been told to you, and to you, O Bhairavī.

items.question: To what kind of person must a particular thing be given according to the conditions stated?
premises: Something is marked as to be given.

items.plain_english: It is to be given to one endowed with all states, to one of resolved mind.

items.question: What restriction applies to giving the Kaula essence when considering its origin in relation to yoginīs?

uncertainties: Exact force of yoginīnām sambhavam remains syntactically open
items.plain_english: The Kaula essence is not to be given; indeed, not what originates from yoginīs.

items.question: In what condition is the speaker's body said to stand today despite its potential for purity?
